title: Who gains?
eyebrow: CETI · a data film · AI at work
lede: One belief, AI makes everyone faster, and three field studies. Pooled, support agents gained 14 % and developers 26 %. Split by skill, the same boxes show a big gain for the least skilled and about none for the most; and 16 experienced developers who expected to be faster were measured slower.

chapters.title: The support desk, pooled and split

captions: Everyone says AI makes everyone faster.
Faster at what, and for whom?
A support desk gave an AI assistant to its agents.
5,179 agents. One box is one agent.
On average: +14 % issues resolved per hour.
Same 5,179 boxes, sorted by skill.
Lowest-skill fifth: +34 %.
Highest-skill fifth: about 0.
The 14 % was a big gain and a flat line, averaged.
Follow one new agent through the split.
Inside the average, her gain was large.
Another test: developers with a coding assistant.
4,867 developers in three field trials.
Pooled: they finished 26 % more tasks.
Newer hires gained more than veterans.
16 experienced developers, on code they know.
246 real issues; AI allowed or banned at random.
They forecast AI would cut their time by 24 %.
Same issues, now timed with a stopwatch.
Measured: 19 % slower.
Afterwards they still believed 20 % faster.
Before you roll AI out, split the gain by experience.
Ask: average gain, or gain for whom?

brand.takeaway: Averages hide who gains. Split by experience first.

sources: Brynjolfsson, Li & Raymond, Generative AI at Work. NBER Working Paper 31161 (QJE 140(2), 2025). 5,179 agents, +14 % issues resolved per hour, +34 % for novice and low-skilled agents, minimal for the most skilled. The journal text reads 5,172 and 15 %.

Cui, Demirer, Jaffe, Musolff, Peng & Salz, The Effects of Generative AI on High-Skilled Work: Evidence from Three Field Experiments with Software Developers. Management Science (2026). 4,867 developers, +26.08 % completed tasks (SE 10.3).

Becker et al. (METR), Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity, 10 Jul 2025; arXiv 2507.09089. 16 developers, 246 issues; forecast 24 % less time, believed 20 % less, measured 19 % more.
METR, We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design, 24 Feb 2026: its follow-up data are very weak evidence; not used for any number here.
honest: Three studies, earlier tools, different tasks; the journal version rounds differently: a pattern, not a law.
